title: Detergent-Free Decellularization of the Human Pancreas for Soluble Extracellular Matrix (ECM) Production
protocol: Prepare 1 L of washing solution consisting of 950 mL of deionized water, 50 mL of iodine-based reagent, and 1% Pen/Strep solution.
Wear sterile gloves and a lab coat during the surgical dissection.
Transfer the pancreas from the sterile transport bag into the sterile placenta basin.
Ensure the pancreas is oriented with the head to the left and the tail to the right.
Carefully dissect the duodenum from the head of the pancreas using sterile scissors and non-toothed forceps.
If a hole is made in the gastrointestinal tract, quickly clamp the hole and proceed with dissection.

Dissect and discard all extra-pancreatic tissue remaining around the head of the pancreas, including major blood vessels and the common bile duct marked at organ procurement time with non-absorbable sutures.
Dispose of the duodenum into an appropriate biohazard bag following institutional guidelines.
Dissect and discard peripancreatic adipose tissue surrounding the tail of the pancreas, exposing splenic blood vessels.

Once the vascular pedicle of the spleen is exposed, remove the spleen and dissect the splenic blood vessels in their entirety, including those attached to the posterior surface of the pancreas (the splenic artery and vein).
Dispose of the spleen and removed tissue following institutional guidelines.
Dissect and dispose any extra-pancreatic fat visible, especially peripancreatic fat.
Lift the retroperitoneum with non-toothed forceps if visible at the level of the tail of the pancreas.
Remove and properly dispose of the lifted retroperitoneal tissue according to surgical standards.
Dissect the pancreas to obtain 1 cm³ cubes of pancreatic tissue using surgical scissors, sterilized histological blades, or surgical scalpels.
Place all dissected pancreatic tissue in a sterile plastic container with washing solution.
Incubate the container at room temperature for 15 min.
Remove the pancreatic tissue from the container using sterile forceps and place it in a new sterile container containing sterile, endotoxin-free deionized water.
Firmly close the cap of the new container.
Place the container on a refrigerated orbital shaker set to 4 °C with shaking speed between 180–200 rpm for 24 h.
Remove the pancreatic tissue using surgical forceps and place it into a new sterile container.
Add 1 L of deionized water, 50 mg of DNase I, and 0.0025% magnesium chloride to the container.
Firmly close the cap of the container.
Place the container in an orbital shaker at 37 °C with shaking speed of 100 rpm for 6 h.
Gather a new sterile 1 L container.
Clean the container appropriately before introducing it into the hood.
To prepare 1 L of EDTA-Trizma solution, add 985 mL of sterile deionized water to the container.
Add 7.5 mL of Tris-HCl Buffer to the container.
Add 7.5 mL of EDTA solution to the container.
Store the prepared EDTA-Trizma solution at 4 °C until use.
Clean the outside of the container enclosing the pancreatic tissue appropriately before introducing it into the hood.
Remove the pancreatic tissue with surgical forceps and place it into a new sterile container with 1 L of EDTA-Trizma-based solution.
Firmly close the cap of the container.
Place the container in an orbital shaker at 4 °C with shaking speed between 180–200 rpm for 18 h.
Remove the container containing the pancreatic tissue and clean the outside appropriately before introducing it into the hood for the process.
Remove the pancreatic tissue with sterile forceps and place it in a new sterile container with sterile endotoxin-free deionized water.
Firmly close the cap of the container.
Place the container on a refrigerated orbital shaker at 4 °C with shaking speed between 180 and 200 rpm for 24 h.
Collect the pancreatic tissue after processing.
Store the collected tissue in sterile 50 mL centrifugation tubes, reaching a maximum of 25 mL per tube.
Freeze the samples and store them at -80 °C.
Transfer the frozen decellularized material into a freeze dryer to perform lyophilization.
Lyophilize the decellularized tissue, ensuring it does not exceed 25 mL in each tube and is frozen at a 45° angle.
Remove lids from lyophilization tubes.
Transfer materials into a cell-culture-grade hood after lyophilization.
Cut each piece of dried ECM into half using sterile scissors.
Subject cut pieces to an automated milling process.
Adjust cryo-milling machine settings to obtain fine powder.
Discard visibly oleaginous tissue post-lyophilization.
Weigh 1 g of ECM powder from an average size pancreas (100 g) using a sterile plastic spatula.
Solubilize 1 g of ECM in 100 mL of 0.01 M HCl and add 100 mg of pepsin for 48 h at room temperature with constant stirring.
Neutralize the pH of the acidic ECM solution with NaOH to achieve a neutral pH (pH = 7) while keeping the beaker on ice.
Transfer the neutralized ECM solution into sterile 50 mL centrifuge tubes.
Centrifuge the tubes containing the solubilized ECM at maximum speed (12,000 x g) for 15 min at 4 °C.
Transfer the supernatant from the centrifuged samples into a cell culture hood.
Using sterile techniques, collect the supernatant of the tube containing the solubilized ECM solution.
Transfer the collected supernatant into fresh 50 mL tubes.
Store the ECM-solution tubes at -80 °C.
Transfer the tubes containing soluble ECM-solution into a freeze dryer after storage for at least 24–40 h at -80 °C.
Ensure that the material does not thaw during transfer to the freeze dryer.
Remove the lids from the falcon tubes before lyophilization.
After complete lyophilization, transfer the material into a cell culture-grade hood.
Observe and collect the fine ECM powder after complete lyophilization.
Store the solubilized ECM powder at 4 °C for immediate use.
Store the ECM powder at -20 °C for later use.
Store the ECM powder at -80 °C for long-term storage.
Collect a piece of native pancreas before decellularization.
Fix the collected pancreas in 10% formalin for 24 hours.
Wash the fixed sample in deionized water.
Dehydrate the washed sample through graded alcohol.
Embed the dehydrated sample in paraffin and slice into 5 μm sections.
Collect a sample of decellularized material at the end of the process.
Fix the collected decellularized material in 10% formalin for 24 hours.
Wash the fixed decellularized sample in deionized water.
Dehydrate the washed decellularized sample through graded alcohol.
Embed the dehydrated decellularized sample in paraffin and slice into 5 μm sections.
Perform H&E staining on both native pancreas and decellularized samples.
Perform DAPI staining on both native pancreas and decellularized samples.
Perform Masson’s Trichrome (MT) staining for histological characterization of collagen structures.
Perform Alcian Blue (AB) staining for histological characterization of GAGs structures.
Quantify DNA content in the native pancreatic tissue and soluble ECM powder.
Analyze total collagen in the native pancreatic tissue and soluble ECM powder.
Measure sulfated glycosaminoglycans (sGAG) content using a commercially available kit.
Use a microplate spectrophotometer to measure sGAG content at 595 nm wavelength.
Reconstitute human pancreatic islets upon arrival for culture.
Culture human pancreatic islets in non-tissue culture treated plates under standard conditions for 24 hours.
Manipulate the cultured islets to test the effect of ECM on functionality and viability.
Cultivate the experimental groups (Free Islets, Alginate-encapsulated Islets, Alginate-ECM encapsulated Islets) under standard conditions for up to 8 days.
Weigh alginate and suspend it in HBSS at a ratio of 1.5% (w/v).
Place the suspension on a rotator overnight at 4°C.
Weigh ECM and suspend it in previously prepared alginate solution to achieve a concentration of 0.1 mg/mL.
Gently collect and mix 3,000 IEQ islets in 1 mL of alginate.
Mix another 3,000 IEQ islets in 1 mL of alginate-ECM at an ECM concentration of 0.1 mg/mL.
Pump suspensions through a microfluidic encapsulation device set to 0.2 mL/min flow rate.
Maintain an air pressure of 2.0 Pa during pumping.
Collect the produced microcapsules in a bath containing 100 mM CaCl2 and 10 mM HEPES.
Allow alginate to crosslink for 10 minutes.
Wash encapsulated islets with HBSS at 37°C and 5% CO2 for 2–3 minutes.
Add culture media to the encapsulated islets as specified in Table of Materials.
Change two-thirds of the media every other day until the end of the experiment.
Perform glucose-stimulated insulin secretion (GSIS) and DNA analysis on day 8 post-encapsulation to assess insulin production and viability.
Obtain brightfield images of free and encapsulated islets for morphological assessment.
Conduct Live/Dead staining to evaluate cellular viability.
Insert gel filtration resin in polypropylene columns.
Insert treatment groups (free islets or encapsulated islets) in the middle portion of the gel filtration resin within the polypropylene columns.
Pipette glucose and depolarizing solutions into the polypropylene columns described above.
Incubate for 1 hour, starting with a pre-incubation period using low molarity glucose solution followed by incubations with low, high, low, and depolarizing glucose solutions in that order.
Collect medium from each incubation phase and store at -80°C for subsequent analysis.
Incubate human pancreatic islets with 1 mL of DNA extraction buffer after the final incubation.
Store the DNA extraction buffer until further analysis.
Measure insulin content from the glucose and depolarizing solution incubations using an Insulin ELISA assay, following manufacturer’s protocol.
Measure DNA content from the extraction buffer collected in step 9.5 using a DNA assay kit according to manufacturer’s protocol.
Normalize insulin measurements according to the DNA content.
